title: What became of Floyd's musicians; Leroy Moore, Alan Vann, John Henry Braggs
summary: Most of Floyd's men have died; Albert got Alan Vann the piano job, quit in 1929, and recalls banjoist John Henry Braggs.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Let me see what else he wrote me, because I'll check Laurie Wright's letter here. What happened to the men with Troy Floyd? I forgot.

Well, it's quite, most of those fellas have passed. Those that are not passed, they are real elderly people now, and I imagine, the last time I saw Benny Long was about three years ago, and Benny's been awful sick. He hadn't had one of his legs cut off. Willie Long is dead. Charlie Dixon is dead. Troy Floyd is dead. The first piano player was named Leroy Moore, and I'm sure that he's gone.
Alan Vann was with him, huh?

Well, I got Alan Vann the job with him after Leroy Moore quit. See, I had a broad amount of, well, I don't know how you put it. Troy had depended on me to do things for him, and I would seek the musician, so I told him about Alan Vann's playing, and Troy was always a fella that you had to prove to him, or he never showed that he never was too interested in what you were talking about. So I had Alan to come and rehearse with the band at 520 South Hagbury, and he took him into the band from there. But I don't remember exactly how long the band stayed, but I think he stayed all the time that I was in the band. I quit the band in 1929, in Fort Worth, Texas.
Well, somebody in that band I was going to ask you about. Well, you only had John Alfred, the drummer. Oh, the guitar player.

Oh, John Henry Braggs. He's still living. He's in San Antonio. He doesn't play anymore. Did he sing the blues ever? No. Just played the banjo. He played an old-style banjo, what they call the plectrum banjo, five strings. Mm-hmm. Good musician. His wife was a blues singer, Ed L. Braggs.
I believe he may have recorded some himself, you know, later on. Maybe. I'll have to look it up.
I don't believe so. I believe after Troy's band disbanded, he might have done something with his wife in Fort Worth.
Yeah. That's what I'm thinking. That was his home, Fort Worth. Mm-hmm. I thought maybe they cut some blues together or something. I don't have the book with me. I don't believe it.
Yeah, they might have. I won't say he didn't.
